results.title: Minimal non-nilpotent subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $M$ of a group $G$ is minimal non-nilpotent if $M$ is not nilpotent but every proper subgroup of $M$ is nilpotent.

results.title: Subgroups permuting with all minimal non-nilpotent subgroups (Kourovka 17.56)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that if $H$ is a subgroup of a finite group $G$ with $HM = MH$ (as sets of products) for every minimal non-nilpotent subgroup $M$ of $G$, then the quotient $H/H_G$ is nilpotent, where the normal core $H_G$ is the largest normal subgroup of $G$ contained in $H$.

results.title: Permutability with minimal non-nilpotent subgroups does not force a nilpotent core quotient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a finite group $G$ and a subgroup $H$ of $G$ with $HM = MH$ (as sets of products) for every minimal non-nilpotent subgroup $M$ of $G$ such that the quotient $H/H_G$ is not nilpotent, where the normal core $H_G$ is the largest normal subgroup of $G$ contained in $H$.

results.title: Schmidt subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Schmidt subgroup when $H$ is not nilpotent but every proper subgroup of $H$ is nilpotent.

results.title: $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal in $G$ when $H = G$ or there is a chain of subgroups $H = H_0 < H_1 < \cdots < H_n = G$ in which every index $|H_i : H_{i-1}|$ is a prime number.

results.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 18.30
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that every finite group in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal is soluble. The problem is due to A. F. Vasil'ev, T. I. Vasil'eva and V. N. Tyutyanov.

results.title: Finite groups with $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal Schmidt subgroups are soluble
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite group in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal is soluble. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 18.30 in the affirmative.

results.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 19.85
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every partition $\sigma$ of the set of all primes into nonempty pairwise disjoint blocks and every finite group $G$ in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\sigma$-subnormal, $G$ has a normal $\sigma$-nilpotent subgroup $N$ such that $G / N$ is cyclic: there is $g \in G$ such that every $x \in G$ satisfies $x g^{-k} \in N$ for some integer $k$. The problem is due to A. N. Skiba.

results.title: Finite groups with $\sigma$-subnormal Schmidt subgroups are $\sigma$-nilpotent-by-cyclic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a partition of the set of all primes into nonempty pairwise disjoint blocks, and let $G$ be a finite group in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\sigma$-subnormal. Then $G$ has a normal $\sigma$-nilpotent subgroup $N$ such that $G / N$ is cyclic: there is $g \in G$ such that every $x \in G$ satisfies $x g^{-k} \in N$ for some integer $k$. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 19.85 in the affirmative.

results.title: Edge relation of an exact covering system digraph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $d_1, \dots, d_r$ and $a_1, \dots, a_r$ be integers. The digraph $G(d_1 n + a_1, \dots, d_r n + a_r)$ has vertex set $\mathbb{Z}$ and an edge $x \to y$ iff $y = d_i x + a_i$ for some $i \in \{1, \dots, r\}$.

results.title: Out-neighbours in a two-rule digraph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all integers $d_1, d_2, a_1, a_2, x, y$, the digraph $G(d_1 n + a_1, d_2 n + a_2)$ has an edge $x \to y$ iff $y = d_1 x + a_1$ or $y = d_2 x + a_2$.

results.title: $k$-descendants in a digraph on the integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$, let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then $n$ is a $k$-descendant of $m$ in $R$ when there is a directed walk of exactly $k$ edges from $m$ to $n$, that is, integers $m = x_0, x_1, \dots, x_k = n$ such that $R$ has an edge $x_{i-1} \to x_i$ for every $1 \le i \le k$.

results.title: Cycles of a digraph on the integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$, given by its edge relation. A list $c = (c_1, \dots, c_t)$ of integers is a cycle of $R$ when it is nonempty, its entries are pairwise distinct, and $R$ has the edges $c_1 \to c_2, \dots, c_{t-1} \to c_t$ and $c_t \to c_1$ (for $t = 1$ this means a loop $c_1 \to c_1$).

results.title: One-vertex cycles of a digraph on the integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$ and let $x \in \mathbb{Z}$. The one-element list $(x)$ is a cycle of $R$ if and only if $R$ has a loop $x \to x$.

results.title: Two-vertex cycles of a digraph on the integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$ and let $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}$. The list $(x, y)$ is a cycle of $R$ if and only if $x \ne y$ and $R$ has both edges $x \to y$ and $y \to x$.

results.title: Translation isomorphism of exact covering system digraphs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$, let $d_1, \dots, d_r$, $a_1, \dots, a_r$ and $k$ be integers, and put $a_i' = a_i - (d_i - 1)k$. Then the map $x \mapsto x + k$ is a digraph isomorphism from $G(d_1 n + a_1, \dots, d_r n + a_r)$ onto $G(d_1 n + a_1', \dots, d_r n + a_r')$.

results.title: Reflection isomorphism of exact covering system digraphs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$, let $d_1, \dots, d_r$, $a_1, \dots, a_r$ and $k$ be integers, and put $a_i' = -a_i + (d_i - 1)k$. Then the map $x \mapsto -(x + k)$ is a digraph isomorphism from $G(d_1 n + a_1, \dots, d_r n + a_r)$ onto $G(d_1 n + a_1', \dots, d_r n + a_r')$.

results.title: Convex bodies in Euclidean space
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a convex body when it is compact and convex and its interior in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is nonempty.

results.title: Covering by translates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For sets $K$ and $L$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ and a natural number $q$, $K$ is covered by $q$ translates of $L$ when there are vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{q} (v_i + L)$, where $v + L = \{v + y : y \in L\}$.

results.title: Covering by interior translates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $q$ interior translates, for a natural number $q$, when there are vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{q} (v_i + \operatorname{int} K)$, where $\operatorname{int} K$ is the interior of $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $v + S = \{v + y : y \in S\}$.

results.title: Uniform bound for covering convex bodies by interior translates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n, q \in \mathbb{N}$, the uniform interior translate bound holds when every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) is covered by $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, that is, $K \subseteq (v_1 + \operatorname{int} K) \cup \dots \cup (v_q + \operatorname{int} K)$ for some $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$.

results.title: Central symmetry about some center

results.title: Covering by smaller positive homothets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $q$ smaller positive homothets, for a natural number $q$, when there are real numbers $r_1, \dots, r_q$ with $0 < r_i < 1$ for every $i$ and vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that every point of $K$ lies in $v_i + r_i K = \{v_i + r_i y : y \in K\}$ for some $i$.

results.title: Translate covering number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For sets $K, L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the translate covering number of $K$ by $L$ is the least natural number $q$ for which there are vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $K \subseteq (v_1 + L) \cup \dots \cup (v_q + L)$, and it is $\infty$ if no such $q$ exists.

results.title: Hadwiger covering number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Hadwiger covering number of dimension $n$, an element of $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, is the least natural number $q$ such that every convex body $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, and it is $\infty$ if no such $q$ exists.

results.title: Symmetric Hadwiger covering number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the symmetric Hadwiger covering number in dimension $n$ is the least natural number $q$ such that every centrally symmetric convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior that is symmetric about some point) is covered by $q$ translates of its interior, and it is $\infty$ if no such $q$ exists.

results.title: Pointwise form of covering by translates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For sets $K$ and $L$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ and a natural number $q$, $K$ is covered by $q$ translates of $L$ if and only if there are vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that every $x \in K$ lies in $v_i + L = \{v_i + y : y \in L\}$ for some $i$.

results.title: Interior-translate covers unfold to translate covers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ and every natural number $q$, $K$ has a cover by $q$ interior translates if and only if $K$ is covered by $q$ translates of the set $L = \operatorname{int} K$, the interior of $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

results.title: The translate covering number is the least covering count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K, L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and let $q \in \mathbb{N}$. If $q$ is the least natural number $r$ such that $K$ is covered by $r$ translates of $L$, then the translate covering number of $K$ by $L$ equals $q$.

results.title: A least uniform bound is the Hadwiger covering number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $q$ is the least natural number such that every convex body $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $q$ translates of its interior, then the Hadwiger covering number of dimension $n$ equals $q$.

results.title: A least uniform bound is the symmetric Hadwiger covering number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $q$ is the least natural number such that every centrally symmetric convex body $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $q$ translates of its interior, then the symmetric Hadwiger covering number of dimension $n$ equals $q$.

results.title: Coordinate cube
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the coordinate cube is the set $[-1, 1]^n$ of points $x$ of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $-1 \le x_i \le 1$ for every coordinate $i$.

results.title: The coordinate cube as an absolute-value box
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$, the coordinate cube in $\mathbb{R}^n$ equals the set of points $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $|x_i| \le 1$ for every coordinate $i$.

results.title: Affine cube
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is an affine cube if $K = e([-1, 1]^n)$ for some affine bijection $e : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$, where $[-1, 1]^n$ is the coordinate cube $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : -1 \le x_i \le 1 \text{ for all } i\}$.

results.title: Interior of the coordinate cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ lies in the interior of the coordinate cube $[-1, 1]^n$ if and only if $-1 < x_i < 1$ for every coordinate $i$.

results.title: The coordinate cube is a convex body
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$, the coordinate cube $[-1, 1]^n$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a convex body: it is compact and convex, and its interior in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is nonempty.

results.title: The coordinate cube is centrally symmetric
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$, the coordinate cube $[-1, 1]^n$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is centrally symmetric: there is a point $c \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $x$ lies in the cube if and only if $2c - x$ does.

results.title: Covering the cube by translates of its interior needs $2^n$ translates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C_n = [-1, 1]^n$ be the coordinate cube in $\mathbb{R}^n$. If $C_n$ is contained in the union of $q$ translates $v_1 + \operatorname{int} C_n, \dots, v_q + \operatorname{int} C_n$ of its interior, then $2^n \le q$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $q$ be natural numbers. If every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) can be covered by $q$ not necessarily distinct translates of its interior, then $2^n \le q$.

results.title: Uniform interior-translate bounds in dimension three are at least eight
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $q$ is a natural number such that every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is contained in the union of $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, then $8 \le q$.

results.title: Lower bound $2^n$ for centrally symmetric interior-translate covering
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $q$ be natural numbers. If every centrally symmetric convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior that is symmetric about some point) can be covered by $q$ not necessarily distinct translates of its interior, then $2^n \le q$.

results.title: Eight translates of the interior cover the three-dimensional cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C_3 = [-1, 1]^3$ be the coordinate cube in $\mathbb{R}^3$. There are vectors $v_1, \dots, v_8 \in \mathbb{R}^3$ such that $C_3$ is contained in the union of the translates $v_1 + \operatorname{int} C_3, \dots, v_8 + \operatorname{int} C_3$ of its interior.

results.title: Eight is the least number of interior translates covering the three-dimensional cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C_3 = [-1, 1]^3$ be the coordinate cube in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Then $8$ is the least natural number $q$ such that $C_3$ is contained in the union of $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} C_3$.

results.title: Translate covering number of the three-dimensional cube by its interior
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C_3 = [-1, 1]^3$ be the coordinate cube in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The translate covering number of $C_3$ by its interior $\operatorname{int} C_3$, the least number of translates of $\operatorname{int} C_3$ whose union contains $C_3$, equals $8$.

results.title: Illumination by a direction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a set and let $v, x \in \mathbb{R}^n$. The direction $v$ illuminates $x$ with respect to $K$ when $x$ lies on the boundary of $K$, $\|v\| = 1$, and $x + tv$ lies in the interior of $K$ for some real $t > 0$.

results.title: Illumination by $q$ directions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is illuminated by $q$ directions, for a natural number $q$, if there are unit vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ (not necessarily distinct) such that for every boundary point $x$ of $K$ there are an index $i$ and a real $t > 0$ with $x + tv_i$ in the interior of $K$.

results.title: Illumination by an external point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a set and let $p, x \in \mathbb{R}^n$. The point $p$ illuminates $x$ with respect to $K$ when $p \notin K$, $x$ lies on the boundary of $K$, and $p + t(x - p)$ lies in the interior of $K$ for some real $t > 1$; that is, the ray from $p$ through $x$ meets the interior of $K$ at a point beyond $x$.

results.title: Illumination by $q$ external points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is illuminated by $q$ external points, for a natural number $q$, if there are points $p_1, \dots, p_q \in \mathbb{R}^n \setminus K$ (not necessarily distinct) such that for every boundary point $x$ of $K$ there are an index $i$ and a real $t > 1$ with $p_i + t(x - p_i)$ in the interior of $K$.

results.title: Directional illumination number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The directional illumination number of a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is the least natural number $q$ such that $K$ is illuminated by $q$ directions, and $\infty$ if there is no such $q$.

results.title: External-point illumination number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The external-point illumination number of a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is the least natural number $q$ such that $K$ is illuminated by $q$ external points, and $\infty$ if there is no such $q$.

results.title: Two equivalent formulations of Hadwiger's covering conjecture
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The following statements are equivalent: for every $n \ge 1$, every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by at most $2^n$ homothets $v_i + r_i K$ with $v_i \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and $0 < r_i < 1$; and for every $n \ge 1$, every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $2^n$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, repetitions allowed.

results.title: Papadoperakis's bound for Hadwiger's covering problem in dimension 3
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is covered by $16$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, repetitions allowed.

results.title: Prymak's bound for Hadwiger's covering problem in dimension 3
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is covered by $14$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, repetitions allowed.

results.title: Lassak's theorem for centrally symmetric bodies in dimension 3
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $8$ is the least natural number $q$ such that every centrally symmetric convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is covered by $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, repetitions allowed. Here $K$ is centrally symmetric when there is a point $c$ with $x \in K$ if and only if $2c - x \in K$.

results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$, let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body and let $q$ be a natural number. results.title: Directional illumination is equivalent to covering by smaller homothets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$, let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body and let $q$ be a natural number. Then some $q$ unit vectors illuminate $K$ if and only if $K$ is covered by $q$ homothets $v_1 + r_1 K, \dots, v_q + r_q K$ with $v_i \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and $0 < r_i < 1$, repetitions allowed.

results.title: Directional illumination is equivalent to covering by interior translates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$, let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body and let $q$ be a natural number. Then some $q$ unit vectors illuminate $K$ if and only if $K$ is covered by $q$ translates $v_1 + \operatorname{int} K, \dots, v_q + \operatorname{int} K$ of its interior, repetitions allowed.

results.title: Directional and exterior-point illumination numbers are equal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the directional illumination number of $K$ equals its exterior-point illumination number. These are the least $q$ such that some $q$ unit vectors, respectively some $q$ points outside $K$, illuminate $K$, with the value $\infty$ when no finite family does.

results.title: Directional illumination number equals the interior-translate covering number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the directional illumination number of $K$ equals the least $q$ such that $K$ is covered by $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$. Both sides take the value $\infty$ when no finite family exists.

results.title: Every convex body has a finite illumination number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ there is a least natural number $q$ such that some $q$ unit vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q$ illuminate $K$: every boundary point $x$ of $K$ has an $i$ and a $t > 0$ with $x + t v_i$ in the interior of $K$.

results.title: Uniform covering by interior translates and uniform directional illumination

results.summary: For integers $n \ge 1$ and $q \ge 0$, every convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) can be covered by $q$ translates of its interior if and only if every convex body $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is illuminated by $q$ directions: there are unit vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q$ such that each boundary point $x$ of $K$ has some $i$ and some $t > 0$ with $x + t v_i$ in the interior of $K$.

results.title: Straight lines in the complex plane
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $s \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is a straight line if there are $a, v \in \mathbb{C}$ with $v \ne 0$ such that $s = \{a + tv : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$.

results.title: Functions whose zeros lie in a given set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has all its zeros in a set $l \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ if every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = 0$ lies in $l$.

results.title: Functions whose ones lie in a given set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has all its ones in a set $m \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ if every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = 1$ lies in $m$.

results.title: Zeros and ones of an entire function on two distinct lines
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: This is the statement that there exist an entire function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and two distinct straight lines $l \ne m$ in $\mathbb{C}$ such that every zero of $f$ lies on $l$, every solution of $f(z) = 1$ lies on $m$, and $f$ has infinitely many zeros and infinitely many solutions of $f(z) = 1$. Here a straight line is a set $\{a + tv : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$ with $a, v \in \mathbb{C}$ and $v \ne 0$.

results.title: Entire functions with zeros and ones on two distinct lines exist
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist an entire function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and two distinct straight lines $l \ne m$ in $\mathbb{C}$ such that every zero of $f$ lies on $l$, every solution of $f(z) = 1$ lies on $m$, and $f$ has infinitely many zeros and infinitely many solutions of $f(z) = 1$. Here a straight line is a set $\{a + tv : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$ with $a, v \in \mathbb{C}$ and $v \ne 0$.

results.title: Chang–Roberts global states
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a ring of $n + 1$ processes $0, \dots, n$, a global state assigns to each process $k$ the FIFO channel of messages waiting at $k$, oldest first, where each message is the index of the process whose identifier it carries, and records for each process whether it has declared itself leader.

results.title: Successor on the Chang–Roberts ring
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: On the ring of $n + 1$ processes $0, \dots, n$, the successor of process $k$ is $k + 1$ when $k < n$, and $0$ when $k = n$.

results.title: Predecessor on the ring
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: On a ring of $n + 1$ processes numbered $0, \dots, n$, the predecessor of $k$ is $k - 1$ if $k \ne 0$, and $n$ if $k = 0$.

results.title: Delivering a message in the Chang–Roberts ring
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: On a ring of $n + 1$ processes with identifiers $\mathrm{id}$, process $k$ receives the oldest message in its channel in state $s$. If the channel of $k$ is empty there is no step. Otherwise let $j$ be the origin of that message, which is removed from the channel: if $\mathrm{id}(k) < \mathrm{id}(j)$, process $k$ forwards it by appending $j$ to the end of the channel of its successor on the ring; otherwise, if…

results.title: The Chang–Roberts transition system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For identifiers $\mathrm{id}$, the algorithm is the labelled transition system whose states are the global states and whose labels are processes: there is a transition from $s$ to $t$ labelled $k$ exactly when delivering the oldest message in the channel of process $k$ in state $s$ gives $t$.

results.title: Initial state of the Chang–Roberts ring
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the initial state the channel into each process $k$ holds exactly one message, whose origin is the predecessor of $k$ on the ring (so every process has sent its identifier to its successor), and no process is leader.

results.title: Reachable states of Chang–Roberts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a natural-number identifier $\mathrm{id}(k)$ for each process $k$ of the ring of $n + 1$ processes, a global state $s$ is reachable when the Chang–Roberts transition system with these identifiers leads from the initial state to $s$ by a multistep transition along some finite list of labels, that is, of receiving processes.

results.title: Forward distance on the ring
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For processes $j$ and $m$ on a ring of $n + 1$ processes numbered $0, \dots, n$, the gap from $j$ to $m$ is the number of successor steps from $j$ to $m$: it is $m - j$ if $j \le m$, and $m + (n + 1) - j$ otherwise. It lies in $[0, n]$.

results.title: Distance travelled by a message
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For processes $j, k$ of the ring of $n + 1$ processes, the distance travelled by a message from $j$ waiting at $k$ is $n + 1$, the whole ring, when $k = j$, and otherwise the ring distance from $j$ to $k$, the number of links from $j$ forward to $k$.

results.title: The Chang–Roberts invariant
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Given identifiers $\mathrm{id}$ on a ring of $n + 1$ processes, a state satisfies the invariant when two conditions hold. First, for every message from origin $j$ waiting in the channel of process $k$, every process $m \ne j$ that the message has already passed has a smaller identifier, $\mathrm{id}(m) < \mathrm{id}(j)$; here $m$ has been passed when its forward distance from $j$ is less than the distance the…

results.title: Forwarding adds one link
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For processes $j$ and $k$ of the ring with $k \ne j$, the distance travelled by a message from $j$ waiting at the successor of $k$ is the number of links from $j$ forward to $k$, plus one.

results.title: The initial messages have travelled one link
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every process $k$ of the ring, the distance travelled by a message from the predecessor of $k$ waiting at $k$ is $1$.

results.title: The Chang–Roberts invariant is preserved along runs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every assignment of identifiers, if the invariant holds in a state $s$ and the state $t$ is reached from $s$ by delivering messages along some schedule of receiving processes (a multistep transition of the algorithm's labelled transition system), then the invariant holds in $t$.

results.title: The Chang–Roberts invariant holds in every reachable state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every assignment of identifiers, every state reachable from the initial state satisfies the invariant.

results.title: Only the maximum is elected
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{id}$ assign a natural-number identifier, not necessarily distinct, to each process $0, \dots, n$ of the Chang–Roberts ring. In every state reachable with these identifiers, if process $i$ has declared itself leader, then $\mathrm{id}(m) < \mathrm{id}(i)$ for every process $m \ne i$.

results.title: There is at most one leader
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In every state of the Chang–Roberts algorithm reachable from the initial state, any two processes that have declared themselves leader are equal.

results.title: Running a delivery schedule
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a natural-number identifier $\mathrm{id}(k)$ for each process $k$ of the ring, a global state $s$ and a list $k_1, \dots, k_r$ of processes, the run applies the Chang–Roberts delivery step at $k_1$, then at $k_2$, and so on. It returns the final state, or no state as soon as some $k_i$ has an empty channel at its turn; on the empty list it returns $s$.

results.title: Runs are multistep transitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Given a natural-number identifier $\mathrm{id}(k)$ for each process $k$ of the ring, for all global states $s, t$ and every list $\kappa$ of processes, running the schedule $\kappa$ from $s$ returns $t$ if and only if the Chang–Roberts transition system with identifiers $\mathrm{id}$ has a multistep transition from $s$ to $t$ labelled by $\kappa$.

results.title: RNA secondary structure
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A secondary structure on `s` (Nussinov et al. 1978): a finite set of base pairs `(i, j)`, each closing a hairpin with at least `m` unpaired positions strictly inside (`i + m < j`), joining complementary bases (`pair s[i] s[j]`, which also puts both positions inside `s`), with every position in at most one pair and no two pairs crossing (`i < k < j < l`).

results.title: Maximum of a list of natural numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The largest of a list of naturals (`0` for the empty list).

results.title: The Nussinov recursion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The first base `a` of `a :: rest` is either unpaired, or paired with `rest[k]` for some `k ≥ m` with `pair a rest[k]`, splitting the rest into the enclosed part `rest.take k` and the outer part `rest.drop (k + 1)`. Exponential-time specification; the usual `O(n³)` table memoizes it on the intervals of `s`.

results.title: Soundness bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every secondary structure has at most `nussinov pair m s` pairs.

results.title: Optimality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Some secondary structure has exactly `nussinov pair m s` pairs, so the recursion computes the maximum number of pairs over all non-crossing structures.
